name: Samuel Eto'o
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2000 Africa Cup of Nations and 2000 Olympic gold with Cameroon at age 19, then became Mallorca's all-time top scorer before joining Barcelona at 23 and scoring in the 2006 Champions League final at 25.
early_history_summary: Eto'o grew up in the New Bell district of Douala, Cameroon, playing street football and joining the Kadji Sports Academy around age 11. Spotted by a Real Madrid scout at 15 in a youth tournament, he moved to Spain in 1996 and joined Real Madrid's youth ranks, was loaned to Leganes, then broke through at Mallorca before his Barcelona move.
family_context_summary: Son of an accountant; the family lived modestly in New Bell, an impoverished district of Douala, and were not rich but lived better than many in Cameroon.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an accountant, not connected to football; mother was a trader. No family domain advantage in football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kadji Sports Academy, Real Madrid youth scouting, precocious talent, street football culture
evidence_summary: Eto'o was scouted by Real Madrid at age 15 from the Kadji Sports Academy in Douala and moved to Spain alone at 16, entering one of the world's elite youth pipelines. His family was modest — father an accountant, mother a trader — with no football lineage, but his precocious physical talent was evident in youth tournaments. He won the Africa Cup of Nations and Olympic gold at 19, became Mallorca's record scorer, and scored in the 2006 Champions League final at 25. The Kadji Sports Academy provided early structured training and exposure to European scouts.
starting_point: Born to an accountant father and trader mother in Douala, Cameroon; family lived modestly in the New Bell district.
current_position: President of the Cameroonian Football Federation (FECAFOOT) since December 2021; retired from professional football in 2019.

trajectory.event: Signed for Real Madrid youth after being scouted at a youth tournament in Cameroon and moved to Spain alone.
Won the Africa Cup of Nations and Olympic gold medal with Cameroon, establishing himself as a global talent.
Joined FC Barcelona from Mallorca, where he had become the club's all-time leading scorer.
Scored in the Champions League final as Barcelona won the title, becoming the second player to score in two UCL finals.
Won a historic treble with Inter Milan under Jose Mourinho, including a second Champions League title.
Elected president of the Cameroonian Football Federation (FECAFOOT).

name: Benoni Beheyt
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1963 UCI World Road Race Championships at age 22, beating compatriot Rik Van Looy in a sprint finish.
early_history_summary: Beheyt won over 100 amateur races from 1958 to 1960 and competed at the 1960 Rome Olympics, finishing seventh in the individual road race. He turned professional in 1962 with Wiel's-Groene Leeuw and immediately won races, culminating in the 1963 World Championship road race title.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Belgian cycling tradition, prolific amateur career, Olympic selection
evidence_summary: Beheyt won over 100 amateur races before turning 20 and competed at the 1960 Rome Olympics, finishing seventh in the road race. He turned professional in 1962 with Belgian team Wiel's-Groene Leeuw and won the 1963 World Championship road race at age 22, outsprinting the great Rik Van Looy. His early development was rooted in Belgium's deep cycling culture, though family background is not documented in available sources.
starting_point: Born in Zwijnaarde, Belgium; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional cycling in 1968; living in Belgium.

trajectory.event: Competed at the Rome Olympics, finishing seventh in the individual road race after winning over 100 amateur races.
Turned professional with Wiel's-Groene Leeuw and won his first professional races.
Won the UCI World Road Race Championships in Ronse, Belgium, outsprinting Rik Van Looy.
Won a stage of the Tour de France and the Tour of Belgium; finished second at Tour of Flanders and Paris-Roubaix.
Retired from professional cycling as results tailed off.

name: Sean Connery
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Connery had minor bit parts in films (Lilacs in the Spring 1955, No Road Back 1956) and chorus/theater roles, but his career-defining breakthrough as James Bond came in 1962 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Connery left school at 15, joined the Royal Navy, then worked as a bodybuilder and model before joining the chorus of South Pacific in 1951. He gained small film roles from 1955 and a TV breakthrough with Requiem for a Heavyweight in 1957, but stardom arrived only with Dr. No in 1962.
family_context_summary: Born in a poor Edinburgh working-class family; left school at 13 and joined the Royal Navy at 16 before being discharged for ulcers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connection to acting or entertainment.
evidence_summary: Connery came from a poor Edinburgh background, left school at 13, and worked various jobs before entering theater via the chorus of South Pacific at 21. His pre-26 film appearances were minor bit parts in quota quickies. His career-defining role as James Bond came at 32 in 1962. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Ornella Muti
milestone_by_age_26: Made her film debut at age 14 in La moglie piu bella (1970) and starred in numerous successful Italian films through the 1970s, achieving wide popularity by her early twenties.
early_history_summary: Born Francesca Romana Rivelli in Rome, she modeled as a teenager to support her family after her father's death. At 14, she accompanied her sister to an audition and was discovered by director Domenico Damiani, who gave her the lead in La moglie piu bella and the stage name Ornella Muti.
family_context_summary: Father was a Neapolitan journalist who died when she was 10; mother was an Estonian sculptor. The family lived modestly and struggled financially after the father's death.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a journalist, providing a modest media/arts household context, but no direct film industry connection is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Discovery by director Damiani, Rome film hub, sister modeling connection, financial hardship catalyst
evidence_summary: Muti was discovered at 14 by director Domenico Damiani while accompanying her sister to an audition in Rome, the center of Italian cinema. Her father, a journalist, had died when she was 10, leaving the family in financial difficulty; she modeled as a teenager to help support the family. Her film debut in La moglie piu bella (1970) was a success and launched a prolific career through the 1970s, culminating in international recognition with Flash Gordon (1980) at age 25.
starting_point: Born in Rome to a Neapolitan journalist father and Estonian sculptor mother; family struggled financially after father's death when she was 10.
current_position: Continues acting in Italian film and television; estimated net worth approximately $10-15 million; resides in Italy.

trajectory.event: Made film debut in La moglie piu bella (The Most Beautiful Wife), discovered by director Domenico Damiani.
Starred in Mario Monicelli's Come Home and Meet My Wife, achieving wide popularity in Italy.
Played Princess Aura in Flash Gordon, gaining international recognition.
Established as one of Italy's most prolific and popular actresses with dozens of film credits.

name: Albert S. Ruddy
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Ruddy was working as an architect in his twenties; his first feature film (Wild Seed) came in 1965 at age 35, and his career-defining work The Godfather came in 1972 at age 42.
early_history_summary: Born in Montreal, Ruddy moved to New York City as a child, graduated from USC, and worked as an architect before entering the entertainment industry in the early 1960s by co-creating Hogan's Heroes. His producing career took off with The Godfather in 1972.
family_context_summary: Born in Montreal, Canada; moved to the US as a child and was raised in New York City. Graduated from University of Southern California.
evidence_summary: Ruddy worked as an architect after graduating from USC and did not enter the film/TV industry until his early thirties. His first feature film was Wild Seed (1965) at age 35, and his career-defining achievement, producing The Godfather, came at 42 in 1972. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Kyros Vassaras
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Vassaras entered refereeing school in 1984 at age 18 but did not become a FIFA-listed referee until 1998 at age 32, with his first senior international in 1999.
early_history_summary: Vassaras was inspired to become a referee by his father, who was also a FIFA referee. He entered the Thessaloniki Referees Association school in 1984 and began officiating matches in 1985, but his international breakthrough came only in 1998 when he was listed as a FIFA referee.
family_context_summary: Father was a football player and later a FIFA referee, which inspired Vassaras to pursue refereeing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a FIFA referee who was a candidate for the 1986 World Cup but missed out due to FIFA cost-cutting; he directly inspired and guided Vassaras's early refereeing career.
evidence_summary: Vassaras entered refereeing school at 18 in 1984, guided by his father who was a former FIFA referee. However, he did not achieve FIFA referee status until 1998 at age 32, well beyond the age-26 threshold. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Miroslav Klose
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Bundesliga debut in April 2000 at age 22, scored 16 goals in the 2001-02 season, and scored 5 goals at the 2002 World Cup at age 24, establishing himself as a top striker.
early_history_summary: Born in Opole, Poland, to professional athlete parents, Klose moved to Germany at age 8. He played for village club SG Blaubach-Diedelkopf from age 9 and trained as a carpenter before joining FC Homburg's reserves at 20 and breaking into the Bundesliga with Kaiserslautern at 22.
primary_leverage_engine: Athletic family background and late-blooming physical talent
family_context_summary: Both parents were professional athletes: father Josef was a professional footballer (Odra Opole, AJ Auxerre) and mother Barbara was a member of the Poland women's national handball team. The family emigrated from Poland to West Germany when Klose was 8.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father played professional football in Poland and France; mother represented Poland in national handball. Both provided direct athletic domain knowledge and inspiration, though the family lived modestly in Germany (father worked as a lathe operator, mother as a cleaner).
primary_early_advantage_tags: Professional athlete parents, football family, immigrant adaptation, German football system
evidence_summary: Klose was born to two professional athletes — his father played professional football for Odra Opole and AJ Auxerre, and his mother was a Polish national handball player. The family emigrated from Poland to West Germany when he was 8, and he grew up in modest circumstances (father a lathe operator, mother a cleaner). He played for a seventh-division village club and was rejected by a sports school for his slight build, making him a late bloomer who reached the Bundesliga at 22. His athletic pedigree and immersion in football culture from birth provided domain proximity, but his path was largely self-created through persistence.
starting_point: Born in Opole, Poland to a professional footballer father and national handball player mother; family emigrated to West Germany when he was 8, living modestly in Kusel.
current_position: Manager of 1. FC Nurnberg in the German 2. Bundesliga; all-time World Cup top scorer with 16 goals.

trajectory.event: Made his Bundesliga debut with 1. FC Kaiserslautern in April 2000.
Scored five goals at the 2002 World Cup including a hat-trick against Saudi Arabia, winning the Silver Boot.
Transferred to Werder Bremen for a 5 million euro fee, establishing himself as a top Bundesliga striker.
Won the World Cup Golden Boot as top scorer and was named German Footballer of the Year.
Won the World Cup with Germany and became the all-time World Cup top scorer with 16 goals.

name: Paul Verhoeven
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Verhoeven made student short films and served as a documentary filmmaker in the Royal Dutch Navy, but his first feature film (Business Is Business) came in 1971 at age 33, and his breakthrough (Turkish Delight) in 1973 at age 35.
early_history_summary: Verhoeven studied mathematics and physics at the University of Leiden, made short films as a student, and served as a documentary filmmaker in the Royal Dutch Navy (1964-66). He moved to Dutch television with the series Floris (1969) before his feature debut in 1971.
family_context_summary: Born in Amsterdam, Netherlands; lived in The Hague during childhood and experienced WWII bombings. Studied mathematics and physics at the University of Leiden.
evidence_summary: Verhoeven made short films as a university student (1960-63) and served as a Navy documentary filmmaker (1964-66), but these were not material career milestones. His first feature film was Business Is Business (1971) at age 33, and his breakthrough Turkish Delight came in 1973 at 35. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Letizia Battaglia
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Battaglia was a housewife and mother in her twenties; she began journalism only in 1969 at age 34 and photography after 1971, with her landmark mafia documentation starting in 1974.
early_history_summary: Born in Palermo, Battaglia was sent to boarding school at 14 and married at 16 to escape. She was a conventional wife and mother of three daughters before divorcing in 1971 and beginning her journalism and photography career in her mid-thirties.
family_context_summary: Born in Palermo, Sicily; sent to boarding school at 14 by her father and married at 16 to Franco Stagnitta, a coffee business owner, to escape her family. Divorced in 1971.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connection to journalism or photography.
evidence_summary: Battaglia was a housewife and mother through her twenties, having married at 16. She began journalism in 1969 at age 34 and photography after her divorce in 1971. Her landmark work documenting the Mafia in Palermo began in 1974 when she was 39. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: David Ortiz
milestone_by_age_26: Made his MLB debut on September 2, 1997 with the Minnesota Twins at age 21, and was the Twins' starting first baseman by 1998, establishing himself as a major-league player well before 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, Ortiz was signed by the Seattle Mariners in November 1992 at age 17 for a small bonus. He worked through the minor leagues, was traded to the Twins organization in 1996, and rocketed from High-A to his MLB debut in September 1997.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and Dominican baseball pipeline
family_context_summary: Born as the oldest of four children to Enrique (Leo) Ortiz and Angela Rosa Arias in Santo Domingo. Father was a car mechanic who had played semiprofessional baseball; mother was a secretary. Parents separated when Ortiz was a teenager. Grew up in the humble community of Haina.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Leo Ortiz played professional and semipro baseball in the Dominican Republic before giving up the sport to support his family as a mechanic. He directly guided Ortiz toward baseball over basketball, arranged training with a buscone, and encouraged English classes at age 13.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Mariners signing, buscone training, father's baseball guidance, Dominican baseball culture, humble origins
evidence_summary: Ortiz grew up in the humble, polluted community of Haina in the Dominican Republic, but his father Leo — a former semipro baseball player — steered him toward baseball and arranged training with buscone Hector Alvarez. Signed by the Mariners at 17 for a minimal bonus, he progressed through the minors and was traded to the Twins, making his MLB debut at 21. The Dominican baseball pipeline and his father's domain knowledge were key early advantages, while his prodigious raw power was noted early by scouts.
starting_point: Born in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic to a car mechanic father (former semipro baseball player) and secretary mother; grew up in the humble community of Haina.
current_position: Retired from MLB in 2016; inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2022; works as a Fox Sports analyst; estimated net worth approximately $55 million.

trajectory.event: Signed by the Seattle Mariners for a small bonus just 10 days after his 17th birthday.
Made his MLB debut with the Minnesota Twins on September 2, after hitting 31 home runs across three minor league levels.
Signed with the Boston Red Sox after being released by the Twins, launching his iconic career.
Won his first World Series with the Red Sox, ending the team's 86-year championship drought.
Won his third World Series and was named World Series MVP.
Inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility.

name: Eiichiro Oda
milestone_by_age_26: Won second place in the Tezuka Award at 17 (1992), worked as assistant to Nobuhiro Watsuki on Rurouni Kenshin at 19, and launched One Piece in Weekly Shonen Jump in July 1997 at age 22, which became the best-selling manga in history.
early_history_summary: Oda resolved to become a manga artist at age 4, influenced by Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball. He began submitting work to Shueisha at 15, won the Tezuka Award at 17, and worked as an assistant to several established mangaka including Watsuki on Rurouni Kenshin before launching One Piece in 1997.
family_context_summary: Born in Kumamoto, Japan; father worked at a firm (office job). Oda decided at age 4 to become a manga artist to avoid a 'real job,' inspired by Fujio Fujiko and later Akira Toriyama.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connection to manga or publishing identified.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tezuka Award, Weekly Shonen Jump, Watsuki mentorship, early submission culture, Toriyama influence
evidence_summary: Oda was singularly focused on manga from age 4, began submitting to Shueisha's Tezuka Award at 15, and won second place at 17, which opened the door to the Weekly Shonen Jump ecosystem. He apprenticed under multiple established mangaka — most notably Nobuhiro Watsuki on Rurouni Kenshin — gaining craft skills and industry access. One Piece launched in July 1997 when Oda was 22 and became the best-selling manga in history. His classmate Nakao introduced him to formal manga tools in junior high, and the Jump award system provided a meritocratic pipeline for young talent.
starting_point: Born in Kumamoto, Japan to an office-worker father; decided to become a manga artist at age 4, inspired by Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball.
current_position: Creator of One Piece, the best-selling manga in history with over 600 million copies in circulation; estimated annual income approximately $23 million; resides in Japan.

trajectory.event: Won second place in the Tezuka Award for his one-shot Wanted!, debuting as a manga artist.
One Piece began serialization in Weekly Shonen Jump issue 34, becoming an immediate hit.
One Piece anime adaptation premiered, expanding the franchise into a multimedia phenomenon.
One Piece reached 100 million tankobon copies sold, cementing its status as a juggernaut.
One Piece certified by Guinness World Records as the best-selling manga series of all time.

name: Judy Tegart-Dalton
milestone_by_age_26: Won her first Grand Slam doubles title at the 1964 Australian Championships at age 26, partnering with Lesley Turner, beginning a career that would yield eight Grand Slam doubles titles.
early_history_summary: Born in Melbourne, Australia, Tegart-Dalton was a serve-volleyer in the Australian tennis tradition. Her first major doubles title came at the 1964 Australian Championships, and she went on to win eight women's doubles Grand Slams, completing a career Grand Slam in doubles.
primary_leverage_engine: Australian tennis ecosystem and doubles specialization
family_context_summary: Born in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Australian tennis tradition, Melbourne tennis hub, Margaret Court doubles partnership
evidence_summary: Tegart-Dalton emerged from Melbourne, the heart of Australian tennis dominance in the mid-20th century. Her first Grand Slam doubles title came at the 1964 Australian Championships at age 26, and she went on to win eight women's doubles Grand Slams — five alongside Margaret Court — completing a career Grand Slam in doubles. Her singles peak came later, reaching the 1968 Wimbledon final at age 30. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources, but the Australian tennis ecosystem provided the pipeline for her development.
starting_point: Born in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional tennis in 1977; served as president of the Fed Cup Foundation; inducted into the Australian Tennis Hall of Fame in 2013.

trajectory.event: Won her first Grand Slam doubles title at the Australian Championships with Lesley Turner.
Reached the Wimbledon singles final, losing to Billie Jean King, and achieved career-high singles ranking of No. 7.
Became one of the Original 9 players who broke away to form the professional women's tennis circuit, later becoming the WTA Tour.
Retired from professional tennis after the Australian Open.
